newsitem.title: UK: Base metals prices steady to softer in quiet LME.
newsitem.headline: Base metals prices steady to softer in quiet LME.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) base metals prices were little changed to easier on Wednesday morning in slow and quiet pre-market trading.
But the market was vulnerable to more of the speculative pressure that dogged most of the complex on Tuesday, traders said.
Three months copper was last quoted at $2,335 per tonne, up just $2 from Tuesday's kerb close.
Copper's proximity to $2,330 suggested a likely re-test of that support level, with next support expected at $2,312, analysts said.
"The speculators are going to dip their toes in again to see what the support is like," a traders said.
Cash/threes backwardation was modestly wider at $42/$47, compared to $35/$40 late on Tuesday.
Traders also noted that tightness in nearby dates were keeping lead and tin in steady backwardations.
In tin, cash/April tightness had encouraged heavy cash buying, pushing cash/threes into a $20/$30 backwardation.
Tin prices were indicated barely softer at $6,010/$6,020 versus Tuesday's kerb close of $6,030.
Lead was down $7 at $701, but was underpinned by a $6/$9 backwardation in the cash/threes from tightness in April and May.
However, lead might edge lower to close a gap between $697 and $694, brokers Brandeis noted.
Aluminium, off $5 at $1,637, was hovering just above nearby support and watching copper for direction.
Support was provided by the 30-day moving average at $1,633 and expectations of buying at $1,625.
Zinc was coming under a bit of speculative pressure on Wednesday morning, and hovering just above the $1,280 level, traders noted.
It was off $5 at $1,285 after losing its grasp on the $1,300 level on Tuesday.
Nickel was barely firmer at $7,920, up $15.
Trade buying had helped underpin nickel since it slipped below $8,000 on Tuesday.
"However, with the close outside of the (symmetrical triangle pattern) and the technical indicators extending down, we should expect further tests of support below $7,900," Rudolf Wolff said.
The market was unaffected by news that Russia's Norilsk Nickel complex would participate in nationwide protests on March 27 but that it would not stop output.
Alloy was last at $1,535 versus $1,530/$1,535.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
